exposure: Neonates born to SARS-CoV-2 infected mothers
Neonates who roomed-in with their mothers
outcome: Clinical characteristics of neonates (meconium-stained amniotic fluid, prematurity, respiratory distress, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, sepsis, hyperbilirubinemia)
cohort: 165 neonates born to SARS-CoV-2 infected mothers at Kalinga Institute of Medical Science (KIMS), Odisha state, India from May 1st to October 20th, 2020.
finding: Vertical transmission of SARS-CoV-2 was observed in 9.4% of cases, but none of the neonates who roomed-in with their mothers and were breastfed developed symptoms of COVID-19.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was more common in mothers with COVID-19.
